svg.title: rEach and Teach: guardrail layers
svg.desc: Nine nested layers surround the AI agent: enrollment lock, sign-in, signed rules and course controls, student consent, qualification, seal and witness ledger, shape and directive check, reply policy and slice fence. Beyond them, Teach runs hidden checks and grading on the server.
svg.text: Nine nested layers around the agent. The last word is not on the student's computer at all.
Every prompt is refused until a security validation pass succeeds and the student enrolls on this
computer. A copied install locks again.
The student ID, a yes and the password open the gates, for 12 hours in any app on this computer.
Wrong tries lock the sign-in out.
No work until the instructors' signed rules verify; offline they hold for 24 hours. Their pauses,
holds and tests are enforced in code.
Nothing is submitted without the student's yes, within 30 minutes, for exactly these files. A
live-session action needs a typed yes too.
A plan audit, scored passes and the agent's own scenarios, here and on Teach. The third failed try
raises a hand; the tenth stops.
Each owned file carries an invisible seal and each session leaves a signed ledger. The server reads
Every change is checked against the course's Dovetail shape and the directive table.
Replies keep code and terminal tasks out of the chat and use everyday words: checked on screen in
Claude Code, corrected after a reply in Claude Code and Codex, guidance elsewhere.
Writes and commands land only inside the student's owned files. rEach's home, other slices and git
hidden checks and grading run on the server, out of the agent's reach
rEach stops accidents and casual tampering. It does not claim to stop a determined
machine owner, which is exactly why the grading happens on Teach.
